findings.title: Denial cache hides newly granted permissions for the whole TTL
Denial cache keyed per resource name can grow without bound
Denial cache key is ambiguous and omits identity type

Explicit-deny test cannot prove the denial cache short-circuits

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Denial cache hides newly granted permissions for the whole TTL

Affected:
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-121
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153-155

Explanation:
The new `Check` flow is built to pick up fresh grants. When the cached permission map does not allow access, it falls back to the database (see the "outdated cache" test).

The denial cache undoes this. Once a deny for `(user, action, name, folder)` is cached, `Check` returns `Allowed: false` at line 117. It never consults the permission cache or the DB for `shortCacheTTL`.

So a user who has just been granted access, or whose dashboard was just moved into an accessible folder, keeps being denied. Nothing invalidates this cache. Users will see "I was given access but still get 403" bugs.

The client-side cache was also removed for in-proc calls, specifically to reduce staleness. That makes this regression more visible.

Fix options:
- Use a much shorter TTL for denials.
- Invalidate denial entries when role, team or permission changes are written.
- Or drop the denial cache and rely on singleflight plus the permission cache.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// in NewService
permDenialCache: newCacheWrap[bool](cache, logger, denialCacheTTL), // e.g. a few seconds
// and/or delete matching denial entries on permission writes
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Performance
Title: Denial cache keyed per resource name can grow without bound

Affected:
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153-155
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32

Explanation:
Every denied `Check` stores one entry per `(namespace, user, action, name, parent folder)`. The values come straight from the request.

A caller that iterates many names or folders, or a large dashboard listing done via per-item checks, creates one local-cache entry per resource. These live in the shared cache that also holds permissions, teams and folder trees.

Before this change, cache size scaled with users × actions. It now scales with users × resources. This raises memory use and cache churn, and gives a cheap way to inflate memory with arbitrary names.

Fix options:
- Bound the cache.
- Use a short TTL.
- Or cache denials at a coarser granularity.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// Prefer a bounded/LRU cache for denials, or skip caching when Name is empty/unknown,
// and keep the TTL short.
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and omits identity type

Affected:
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32

Explanation:
The key is built as `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent>` with `_` separators. Resource names, folder UIDs and user UIDs may themselves contain `_`. Different `(name, parent)` or `(uid, action, …)` tuples can therefore produce the same key and cause false denials.

The key also shares the `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>` prefix used by `userPermCacheKey`, in the same underlying cache. That makes accidental overlaps with a different value type (`bool` vs `map[string]bool`) possible.

The identity type is also not part of the key. Anonymous/render identities and users therefore share a key space keyed only on UID.

Use a dedicated prefix and an unambiguous encoding, such as length-prefixed values or a separator that cannot occur in UIDs.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
func userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, idType, userUID, action, name, parent string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s.perm_denial_%s:%s|%s|%d:%s|%d:%s",
		namespace, idType, userUID, action, len(name), name, len(parent), parent)
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Cached-deny path does duplicate work and records a cache hit as a miss

Affected:
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123-137

Explanation:
When cached permissions exist but do not allow access, `Check`:
- resolves user identifiers again inside `getIdentityPermissions`,
- re-runs the DB permission fetch, and
- evaluates `checkPermission` a second time.

That is roughly double the work on every first-time deny.

It also increments `permissionCacheUsage{"false"}` even though the cache was hit. This skews the hit/miss metric that this PR reorganizes.

Errors from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (for example a DB error from `GetUserIdentifiers`) are silently treated as a miss. Consider distinguishing `cache.ErrNotFound` from real errors.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
cachedPerms, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)
switch {
case err == nil:
	s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("true", checkReq.Action).Inc()
	// ... check, return if allowed
case !errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound):
	ctxLogger.Warn("cache lookup failed", "error", err)
	s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()
default:
	s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Cache lookup removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions affects all callers

Affected:
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:379-380
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:423-424

Explanation:
`getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` no longer read `permCache`. They only write it. Any caller of `getIdentityPermissions` other than `Check` and `List` now always hits the database. Such callers cannot be seen in this diff and would need checking.

The test case covering the cache-hit behavior was deleted rather than moved. The read/write split between `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and these functions is also easy to misuse.

Verify there are no other callers. Otherwise keep a cache-aware wrapper.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// Either document that getIdentityPermissions is "force refresh" only,
// or provide getIdentityPermissionsCached() used by all non-Check callers.
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Explicit-deny test cannot prove the denial cache short-circuits

Affected:
- pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:981-982

Explanation:
The comment says the permission cache is populated to "Allow access … to prove this is not checked". However, the map value is `false`, so the cached permissions do not grant access.

With the denial cache removed, `Check` would still fall back to the default store (no permissions) and deny. The test therefore passes regardless of the denial-cache logic.

Set the value to `true` so that a passing test actually demonstrates the short-circuit. Also add a test asserting that a DB-backed deny populates `permDenialCache`.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
s.permCache.Set(ctx, userPermCacheKey("org-12", "test-uid", "dashboards:read"), map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true})
~~~

This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.

While the candidate frames it as 'duplicate work' rather than explicitly calling out the security risk of stale cached grants, it's pointing to the exact same underlying code logic issue: the asymmetric treatment of cached permission grants vs denials.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
